text:
maria: Heads-up — prepping private/VPC installer bundle for 1.4.3. Packaging found a lint failure in release_notes.md (typo + missing component tags). Need decision: pause packaging and fix before cut, or ship and patch notes post-cut? :thinking:

deploy-bot: Scheduled release window: 2026-03-21T22:00Z -> canary 22:00-22:30, full rollout 22:30-23:00. Lock acquired on staging artifacts. :lock:

sam: Is the lint just formatting (line wrap) or missing required entries? If formatting-only we can auto-fix with the release-notes linter and re-run packaging quickly.

maria: It's two things: a missing component tag (security-policy) which our release-notes lint treats as required for Private builds, and one wrapped line that breaks parsing for the release-notes generator. The registry tag in the bundle is fine.

jordan: For timeline — do not want to delay deploy unless we need to. Can we pin the installer image (1.4.3-rc.2) and ship the binary, then push a tiny release-notes patch (1.4.3+notes) that doesn't change hash? Ops: is that allowed with cosign signatures?

ops: You can push a release-notes patch as separate artifact; you cannot change signed installer image after cosign. If we must change the installer manifest, we need resign and re-escrow. Recommended: ship signed installer as-is if binary hash is correct, and publish corrected release_notes.md as a sidecar artifact with its own signature. We'll stash the new sidecar under s3://redwood-escrow/private/1.4.3/release-notes-v1.sig

rei: We should define rollback criteria now if we decide to ship. My proposal: canary failure = >2% error rate OR median app-start latency increase >120ms OR packaging agent reports checksum mismatch on >=3 customers. If any trigger hit in canary window, immediate rollback to 1.4.2 pinned.

ben: Also add a health-check for KV cache warmup — we've seen warmup paths fail when new runtime kernels land. If cache-miss rate >10% after 10 minutes, treat as degraded.

maria: Good call. I'll add the two checks to the deploy checklist. Also adding a lint-and-fix preflight script: ```
# run from packaging/
./tools/release-lint --require-tags security-policy,installer
git checkout -b release/1.4.3-lint-fix && ./tools/release-lint --autofix && git commit -am "chore(release): fix release notes lint" && ./scripts/build-installer.sh
```

sam: How long to run that locally and re-run cosign? Packaging time estimate?

maria: Autofix + rebuild + sign ~18-25 minutes if nothing else blocks. Cosign sign + escrow push ~5 minutes. So total ~30 minutes. If we do that, we push new signed bundle and cancel current lock; deploy-bot will need to pick up new thread.

deploy-bot: Current lock TTL: 40 minutes. If you push a new cosign-signed bundle, please ping @deploy-bot with `release: new-bundle 1.4.3` and I will refresh canary window assignment.

jordan: Alternative (faster): ship binary now, publish sidecar notes as ops suggested. Slightly messy but keeps schedule. Do we have compliance constraints that require release-notes to be part of signed payloads for private customers?

ops: For most Private customers we ship an escrowed signed manifest + sidecars. Compliance customers flagged in the contract (list: acme-corp, healthco) require release-notes embedded in the signed manifest. Check contract list before choosing sidecar route.

maria: I checked — two enterprise customers require embedded notes. That means if we don't embed, we must notify them and delay. Not great.

sam: Given that, my vote: do the lint autofix and rebuild. Delay is 30 minutes but gives clean artifacts. Who is OK to run the sign + escrow?

ben: I can run the cosign signing tomorrow if needed, but tonight I'm on call. @maria can you coordinate with @ops to ensure S3 escrow path and signer key TTL? Cosign key TTL currently set to 24h; we need to ensure rotation won't expire mid-escrow.

ops: Confirmed: signer TTL good. I'll create escrow prefix s3://redwood-escrow/private/1.4.3/ and set object ACL to rw for packaging-bot and ops-service. Also will snapshot the cosign attestation and put checksum file: installer-1.4.3.tar.gz.sha256.asc

maria: I'll run autofix now and post progress. If I run into anything blocking, I'll abort and we'll fall back to sidecar + customer-notify. :ok_hand:

maria: (20m later) autofix done, rebuilt installer, running unit smoke: ```
./scripts/installer-smoke --bundle dist/installer-1.4.3.tar.gz
# smoke passed: basic install + health checks
```

maria: Signing now with cosign, uploading to escrow. pinging deploy-bot after upload. :rocket:

deploy-bot: Received `release: new-bundle 1.4.3` from maria. Canaries reassigned, new window preserved. Good luck. :tada:

jordan: Nice. Document the small change in release notes as changelist entry and mark as 'docs-only fix' in changelog so ops/compliance reviewers can see it at quick glance.

maria: Done. Pushed signed sidecar and embedded manifest update. Final checks passed. Closing loop: release moving to canary at 22:00Z. If anyone wants to add a rollback trigger, speak now.

rei: I'll watch canary metrics. If we see error spike or latency drift, I'll call rollback within first 10 minutes.

ben: I'll keep an eye on cosign attestations and escrow checksum. If anything mismatches, abort rollout and cut emergency unpin.

ops: Escrow checksum file: s3://redwood-escrow/private/1.4.3/installer-1.4.3.tar.gz.sha256.asc

maria: Thanks all. :heart:
